title: しか: the inverted selection
summary: しか picks a noun and then makes everything else the subject, which is why the verb must be negative.

blocks.text: **しか** looks like a simple "only", but its structure is unusual. Think of the invert button in a photo editor: you select an object, press invert, and now everything *except* it is selected. That is what しか does with the **A-car**.
私しかいない。 Nobody other than me is here.

The A-car is not 私 but "everyone except me", and the engine says that group is **not** here. That is why しか always needs a negative engine. Like か, しか pushes out が (we never say がしか). It also selects for relevance: it means "no other people", not "no trees or birds either".
A counter works as an adverb. When しか marks it, it flips the amount, not the subject.

blocks.jp: コップが一つしかない。

blocks.text: The subject (コップ) stays; しか takes "one" and inverts it to "every amount but one", and those do not exist.
In speech しか can follow a whole action: "every other course of action does not exist", i.e. "there is nothing for it but to ...".

blocks.en: I have no choice but to go to bed.

items: **しか** selects a noun, then flips it: everything else is the A-car.
しか replaces が and を, but keeps other particles (駅でしか).

questions.instruction: What must the engine of a しか sentence be?
questions.note: しか flips the A-car, so the engine says that group is not here.
しか needs a negative engine: ない.
questions.en: I have only 1000 yen in my bag.

questions.prompt: 箱にりんごが二つ＿＿ない。
questions.note: A counter marked by しか flips the amount.
questions.en: There are only two apples in the box.

questions.prompt: しか always needs a negative engine.
questions.note: The engine says everyone except the selected one is not here.
Like か, しか pushes out が.
Everyone except Yamada does not exist.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I have only one pen"?
questions.note: A counter + しか + a negative engine.

questions.instruction: Which two particles does しか usually take the place of?
questions.note: しか replaces が and を but keeps other particles.

questions.instruction: Which one means "I can buy it only at the station"?
questions.note: で is kept, and しか goes after it with a negative engine.

questions.prompt: りんごが三つしかない。
questions.note: しか takes "three" and inverts it to every other amount, which do not exist.
Verb + しかない: nothing for it but to.
questions.en: There is nothing for it but to go home.

options: I have no choice but to do it
questions.note: Every other course of action does not exist.
questions.en: There is nothing to do but do it.

questions.instruction: Does the sentence say the desks and chairs are absent?
questions.prompt: 教室には先生しかいなかった。
options: No: it means no other people
questions.note: しか selects for relevance: other people, not furniture.
questions.en: There was only the teacher in the classroom.

questions.note: 野菜 is taken, and everything else is flipped.
飲まない is the negative engine that しか needs.
questions.en: My older sister drinks only water.

questions.note: The counter 一つ is marked by しか.
questions.en: There is only one bank near the station.
